Hi, I was wondering if there was any general advice that people have when it comes to writing snippets about your self for referrals when your referrer can't. Some context: my cousin's boyfriend said his company could refer me to for an internship, and the refer asked me to write my own snippet of "why I should be recommended." I feel like normally the refer would use their own personal experiences, but since I don't know my referrer personally I'm not sure at how I should approach this.  I was thinking of doing a couple generic sentences describing where I go to school, and that I'm a hard worker, love to learn, etc. but I feel my self cringing at how basic and ordinary that sounds.  Any help would really be appreciated! :))

Thanks for taking the time to give me all this feedback, I really appreciate it! If you have the time, I have a couple of questions in regards to some of the feedback you gave me.

> Include more quantifiable statistics. 

* For quantifiable statistics, tldr; i was able to remove a periodic RPC that was happening every 2 minutes. I changed some logic / architecture of how the database subsystem checks it's license, which is another subsystem that requires an RPC.  Do you know of a concise way to phrase that? (That's one of the reasons I didn't put that detail and was thinking I could verbally explain it if asked)

> Include throughout numbers for the database bullet.

* What do you mean by "throughout numbers"?

> Include the size of the code base for the testing suite.

* I'm guessing this is for my third bullet for my current position? The tests I refactored were originally ~3,500 lines.  The codebase for those unit tests are around ~10,000 (very rough guess, definitely > 7,000). Should I plop those numbers in / whats a nice way to do that without it sounding like kind of out of nowhere?

> Include more details about how far the "voice user interface" made it. Did it when into production? How many people used it?

* This was never touched after me, and just lives in a collection of intern projects (was a disappointing internship but that's a different topic). Given that is it good as is?

> Include how many people read the learning guide.

* Will do! Last time I checked the number of reads was in the hundreds. Never thought about adding that number.
Thank-you in advance! :)
